extracted.intended_audience: USPTO management, auditors, congressional stakeholders, and other users of USPTO financial statements and operational policies (including agency staff and external stakeholders interested in USPTO accounting and reporting)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies, definitions, and accounting/reporting standards used by the USPTO to prepare consolidated financial statements and related notes for fiscal years 2016 and 2015, including revenue recognition, capitalization, liabilities, and other significant accounting policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The accompanying financial statements present the financial position, net cost of operations, budgetary resources, and cash flows for the USPTO’s goals as required by the Chief Financial Officers Act of 1990 and 31 U.S.C. §3515(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements were prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP), the form and content specified by OMB Circular No. A-136, and Federal Accounting Standards set by the Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board (FASAB). Books and records of the USPTO serve as the source; presentations may differ from other OMB reports prepared for budgetary control purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of Accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements reflect both accrual and budgetary accounting transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under accrual accounting, revenues are recognized when earned and expenses when incurred. Budgetary accounting recognizes obligation of funds according to legal requirements (often before accruals). Budgetary accounting is essential for compliance with legal constraints and controls over federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds from Dedicated Collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds from dedicated collections are financed by specifically identified revenues that remain available over time and are required by statute to be used for designated activities, benefits, or purposes and accounted for separately from general revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the USPTO these include the salaries and expenses fund, fee reserve fund, and special fund receipts. Additional details provided in Note 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary Activities Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiduciary activities are not recognized on the financial statements but are reported on schedules in the notes to the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiduciary balances are not assets of the federal government. Examples at USPTO include the Patent Cooperation Treaty fund and the Madrid Protocol fund; additional details are in Note 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect reported amounts and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual results could differ from these estimates; management must disclose significant estimates and related uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange Revenue / Revenue Recognition for Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO records fees (exchange revenue) under fee setting authority granted by the Leahy–Smith America Invents Act (AIA) Section 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees remitted with initial applications and service requests are recorded as exchange revenue when received, with an adjustment to defer revenue for services not yet performed. Amounts remitted without a request for service are recorded as liabilities in customer deposit accounts until services are ordered. The Director may set or adjust fees to recover aggregate estimated costs and may set individual fees at, below, or above cost provided aggregate recovery is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputed Financing Sources and Imputed Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: When operating costs are paid in full or in part by other federal entities, the USPTO includes applicable imputed costs and recognizes an imputed financing source from costs absorbed by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include CSRS pension benefits paid by OPM, certain legal judgments paid from the Judgment Fund, and the cost of electronic fee collection paid by Treasury. These are included on the Consolidated Statements of Net Cost and Changes in Net Position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity vs Non-Entity Assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Entity assets are those an entity is authorized to use in its operations; non-entity assets are held but not available for the entity’s use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most USPTO assets are entity assets; a portion of the Fund Balance with Treasury and cash may be non-entity. Additional details provided in Note 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund Balance with Treasury Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds collected are deposited in commercial bank accounts maintained by Treasury’s Bureau of the Fiscal Service and transferred to the Federal Reserve Bank the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many customer deposits are wired directly to the Federal Reserve. Banking activity follows BFS directives and Treasury processes disbursements. More detail in Note 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounts Receivable Policy and Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts receivable are established for amounts owed to the USPTO from employees and some customers; most revenue is collected prior to service so receivables are a small portion of assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An allowance is established for receivables considered not collectible—offsets for receivables older than two years with little/no collection activity that have been transferred to Treasury. Intergovernmental receivables are regarded as fully collectible. See Note 3 for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances and Prepayments
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepayments are recorded when amounts are paid in anticipation of future benefits; expense is recorded when goods are received or services performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO has prepayments with both non-governmental and governmental vendors; details are in Note 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash and Cash Equivalents Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash balance primarily consists of checks, electronic funds transfers, and credit card payments in transit and undeposited checks not yet credited to Fund Balance with Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undeposited checks are considered cash equivalents. Cash held outside the Treasury is used as imprest funds. See Note 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property, Plant, and Equipment Capitalization and Depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes of property and capitalization thresholds determine which acquisitions are capitalized; costs capitalized at historical cost and depreciated on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization thresholds (individual purchases / bulk purchases) include: IT Equipment/Software/Software in Progress/Furniture/Equipment/Leasehold Improvements generally $50k individual / $250k bulk (leasehold improvements: $50k individual, bulk N/A). Leasehold improvements depreciated over remaining lease life or useful life, whichever is shorter. Useful lives updated prospectively; additional details in Note 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of Contractor Costs for Internal Use Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor costs for developing custom internal-use software are capitalized when incurred for design, coding, and testing of the software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software in progress is not amortized until placed in service; costs that do not meet capitalization criteria are expensed upon receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workers’ Compensation Accounting (FECA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims under the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act (FECA) are administered by the Department of Labor (DOL) and ultimately paid by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOL bills USPTO annually as claims are paid but payment is deferred ~two years for budget funding. Actuarial liability is estimated using actuarial procedures including incurred-but-not-reported (IBNR) components and updated annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unemployment Compensation Accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Unemployment compensation benefits under the DOL-administered program are billed to agencies quarterly as claims are paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO recognizes the quarterly billing process by DOL; amounts are recorded as the claims are paid and billed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual, Sick, and Other Leave Accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual leave and compensatory time are accrued as earned and reduced when taken; sick leave and other non-vested leave are expensed as used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances in accrued leave accounts are adjusted each fiscal quarter to reflect current pay rates. No portion of annual leave liability has been obligated; if current funding unavailable, funding will be obtained from future financing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee Retirement and Post-Employment Benefits Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees participate in CSRS or FERS; USPTO financial statements do not report CSRS/FERS assets or plan liabilities—those are reported by OPM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO recognizes a funded expense for its share of costs to the federal government and recognizes an imputed cost for OPM’s share. The USPTO’s appropriation requires full funding of present costs as determined by OPM for FEHB, FEGLI, and CSRS pensions; ultimate administration remains with OPM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation Transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation transfers are delegations by one department of authority to obligate budget authority and outlay funds to another department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO does not receive any allocation transfers.
